article_content: Sao Paulo has confirmed the signing of Brazilian playmaker Paulo Henrique Ganso from Santos for a reported $12 million. The 22-year-old midfielder agreed to a five-year contract after the clubs reached an agreement. Ganso made 26 appearances this year, hampered by knee and muscle injuries.  He previously missed seven months of the 2010 season due to left knee surgery. Alongside Neymar, Ganso helped Santos win the 2010 Brazilian Cup and the 2011 Copa Libertadores.  Sao Paulo football director Adalberto Baptista told the club website: 'Ganso demonstrated a strong desire to join Sao Paulo throughout the negotiations. He made sacrifices and remained firm in his objective. Without his persistence, we might have given up.'  'It's a dream come true,' Ganso reportedly told the Associated Press. 'Since Sao Paulo expressed interest, I've wanted this deal. I'm eager to play and repay the club's efforts.' Santos negotiated a 5% sell-on fee after initially resisting selling Ganso to a rival.  European clubs, including Inter Milan, Manchester United, and Tottenham Hotspur, reportedly showed interest, but no formal offers materialized. Ganso's desire to leave was clear, prompting fan protests.  A salary disparity with Neymar reportedly influenced his decision.  Ganso aims to revitalize his career after injuries and a dip in form, which cost him a spot in Brazil's Olympic squad, where he was replaced by Chelsea's Oscar.  With the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, Ganso hopes to impress national coach Mano Menezes.

'מאז שסאו פאולו הביעה עניין, רציתי שהעסקה תצא לפועל. אני משתוקק לשחק ולגמול למועדון על מאמציו'. סנטוס ניהלה משא ומתן על דמי מכירה של 5% לאחר שהתנגדה בתחילה למכור את גאנסו ליריבה. מועדונים אירופיים, כולל אינטר מילאן, מנצ'סטר יונייטד וטוטנהאם, גילו עניין, אך לא הוגשו הצעות רשמיות. רצונו של גאנסו לעזוב היה ברור, מה שעורר מחאות אוהדים. פער בשכר עם ניימאר השפיע, ככל הנראה, על החלטתו. גאנסו שואף להחיות את הקריירה שלו לאחר פציעות וירידה בכושר, מה שעלה לו במקום בסגל האולימפי של ברזיל, שם הוחלף על ידי אוסקר מצ'לסי. עם מונדיאל 2014 בברזיל, גאנסו מקווה להרשים את מאמן הנבחרת מאנו מנזס.

article_content: 'Following President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi's departure from Sanaa, four Gulf nations have established embassies in Aden, Yemen.  The UAE and Kuwait opened their embassies on Friday, according to two Foreign Ministry officials close to Hadi.  This follows Saudi Arabia and Qatar relocating their embassy staff to Aden the previous day.  Yemen's capital, Sanaa, remains under Houthi rebel control. Hadi, who escaped house arrest a week after resigning under pressure, insists he is still Yemen's legitimate president.  From Aden, he declared all political decisions since September null and void.  An official indicated Egypt may also open an embassy in Aden soon.  Citing Aden's calm security situation, the Saudi ambassador to Yemen explained the difficulty of operating in Sanaa. Political talks, facilitated by the UN, collapsed Friday as most parties withdrew, demanding a location free from militant threats.  U.N. envoy Jamal Benomar confirmed Hadi's constitutional presidency during a visit, emphasizing his crucial role in resolving the crisis.  Hadi has stipulated that talks must relocate from Sanaa before his involvement. The Houthis, a Shiite Muslim group feeling marginalized in the Sunni-majority country, have strengthened their hold on power.  Their decade-long conflict with the government escalated with their September takeover of Sanaa, leading to deadly clashes and a subsequent ceasefire.  The Houthi's takeover of Sanaa, and Hadi's refusal to comply with certain demands, led to political unrest and prompted the resignation of Hadi under duress last month, after which he fled the capital, and the withdrawal of diplomatic staff by Western nations including the United States and several European and Gulf countries.'

The quake originated at a depth of 10 kilometers (6.2 miles). The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center confirmed no tsunami threat, echoing the Japan Meteorological Agency, which briefly advised of potential strong currents before withdrawing the advisory.  Tokyo Electric Power Company, operator of the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant, reported no irregularities at its facilities following the tremor.'

article_content: While fasting diets like the 5:2 method have shown promise in promoting longevity and improving health markers such as blood pressure, new research raises concerns about potential downsides. A study conducted by scientists at the University of Bath, using fruit flies as a model, suggests that fasting could increase vulnerability to infections. The research team, led by Dr. Nick Priest, found that while fasting extended the lifespan of fruit flies exposed to a fungal disease by approximately 14%, it also led to a 20% increase in their susceptibility to infection. The scientists observed a correlation between genes activated by fungal infection in flies and those activated in humans during periods of dietary restriction.  This raises the possibility that similar trade-offs between longevity and immunity might exist in humans following fasting diets.  Although the benefits of caloric restriction are well-documented, Dr. Priest emphasizes the need for more research into the long-term health consequences, particularly concerning immune function.  He noted previous studies demonstrating increased infection risk in starved mice. While acknowledging the potential health advantages of intermittent fasting, he cautions that these diets are not without potential drawbacks.  Further investigation is needed to fully understand the mechanisms behind these observations and their implications for human health.

article_content: 'A wealthy New York City couple, previously accused of enslaving and abusing their nanny, have been barred from re-entering the US. A border official cited their case as potential human trafficking, despite the couple being cleared of the charges.  Malu Custer Edwards, 30, and Micky Hurley, 37, of Chilean aristocratic descent, spent a year in court denying the allegations made by their nanny, Felicitas del Carmen Villanueva Garnica. Garnica claimed she was forced to work long hours for low pay and subjected to abuse in their Upper East Side apartment. However, a judge dismissed the case in December, citing inconsistencies in Garnica's testimony. Despite the dismissal, Edwards, Hurley, and their three young children remain in Portofino, Italy. Edwards, whose ancestor Agustín Edwards Mac-Clure led the League of Nations, expressed her frustration to the New York Times, stating their unexpected extended stay in Italy has disrupted their lives. They are appealing the decision and seeking a new rental apartment in New York. The couple also reported receiving hate mail and death threats, according to the New York Post. They maintain their innocence and desire to return to their lives in New York. The lawsuit was dismissed after Judge Alvin Hellerstein found contradictions in Garnica's testimony.  The New York Department of Labor previously ordered the couple to pay Garnica back wages, related to a separate labor dispute. Garnica had also alleged to the New York Post that the couple restricted her food while frequently dining at expensive restaurants. The couple's attorney denied these claims.'

article_content: 'In a disturbing trend of animal cruelty, a pregnant goat named Dora was found shot by an arrow in Western Sydney. This marks the fourth such incident in the area this month, following attacks on two other goats, a kangaroo, and a pelican.  Dora, who is expecting twins, was discovered by her 76-year-old owner on their Davis Road property. Thankfully, despite the arrow lodged in her shoulder, Dora is expected to make a full recovery and give birth any day now. The RSPCA confirmed Dora's pregnancy and stable condition after providing initial emergency care.  Local police, including Inspector Steve Thomas, are actively investigating and urging anyone with information to contact Crime Stoppers.'

article_content: 'Google co-founder Sergey Brin expressed his discomfort with smartphone usage, calling it 'emasculating' during a TED conference in Long Beach. He criticized the hunched posture and constant screen interaction associated with mobile phones, suggesting that Google Glass offers a less intrusive alternative. Brin, often seen sporting Google Glass, envisions a future where information is readily available without the need for constant phone checking. However, he admitted to his own mobile phone addiction, describing it as a 'nervous tic'. Public reaction to Brin's remarks was divided, with some questioning his word choice and proposed solution. While some agree with his concerns about excessive phone use, others argue that wearing a computer display on your face is not the answer. The Google Glass project, a wearable computer priced around $1,500, aims to address these concerns by providing hands-free access to information. Google released a video showcasing Glass's features, including taking pictures, recording videos, and displaying directions. Concerns regarding potential health risks associated with wearable technology have also surfaced, particularly about cellular radiation exposure.  Brin cautioned against trusting eBay listings for Google Glass prototypes and confirmed that the device would be publicly available later this year. Google is also collaborating with Warby Parker to develop more stylish frames for Glass.'

article_content: The Eastern Underground Orchid (Rhizanthella slateri), a rare and unusual plant found in only ten locations in New South Wales, Australia, produces spectacular creamy white and purple flowers despite growing entirely underground. Unlike most orchids, it lacks chlorophyll and relies on a symbiotic fungus for nutrients and water, according to Greg Steenbeeke, a senior threatened species officer at the NSW Office of Environment and Heritage.  The orchid consists of several small, potato-like tubers beneath the surface, from which a white stem, about 15cm long and 1.5cm wide, extends upwards, culminating in a glistening flower just above ground level.  'The flower is a dense head, similar to a Waratah but only the size of a 20 cent coin,' Mr. Steenbeeke explains. 'The flowers themselves are a creamy white, translucent, and speckled with purple.'  Because it grows almost entirely underground, the orchid is difficult to detect and is usually discovered only when the soil is disturbed.  Samples have been sent to Leiden, Netherlands, for genetic analysis to better understand its relationship to other non-photosynthesizing plants. The orchid is currently classified as 'vulnerable' due to the long-term threat of extinction.  'This research is important because the orchid's habitat requirements are poorly understood,' says Mr. Steenbeeke.  While the orchid's lack of above-ground parts conserves water, the evolutionary pressures that led to this adaptation remain a subject of study.  Three other chlorophyll-free orchid species exist in Australia, two in Western Australia and one other in the eastern states. This is the first to be sent to the Netherlands for genetic testing, although another species has also had its DNA sampled.  While such underground orchids are found globally, Mr. Steenbeeke notes their relative rarity.
translated_content: סחלב הקרקע המזרחי (Rhizanthella slateri), צמח נדיר ומיוחד שנמצא רק בעשרה מקומות בניו סאות' ויילס, אוסטרליה, מייצר פרחים מרהיבים בצבע לבן-קרם עם נקודות סגולות, למרות שהוא גדל כולו מתחת לאדמה. שלא כמו רוב הסחלבים, הוא חסר כלורופיל ותלוי בפטרייה סימביוטית לצורך הזנה ומים, כך מסביר גרג סטנביק, קצין בכיר למינים בסכנת הכחדה במשרד הסביבה והמורשת של ניו סאות' ויילס. הסחלב מורכב מפקעות קטנות דמויות תפוח אדמה מתחת לפני השטח, מהן צומח גבעול לבן, באורך של כ-15 ס"מ וברוחב של כ-1.5 ס"מ, כלפי מעלה, ומגיע לשיאו בפרח נוצץ ממש מעל פני הקרקע. 'הפרח הוא תפרחת צפופה, הדומה לוורטה, אך בגודל של מטבע של 20 סנט בלבד', מסביר מר סטנביק. 'הפרחים עצמם בצבע לבן-קרם, שקופים ומנוקדים בסגול'. מכיוון שהוא גדל כמעט כולו מתחת לאדמה, קשה לאתר את הסחלב והוא מתגלה בדרך כלל רק כאשר האדמה מופרעת. דגימות נשלחו לליידן, הולנד, לצורך ניתוח גנטי כדי להבין טוב יותר את הקשר שלו לצמחים אחרים שאינם מבצעים פוטוסינתזה. הסחלב מסווג כיום כמין "פגיע" בשל סכנת ההכחדה ארוכת הטווח. "המחקר הזה חשוב משום שדרישות בית הגידול של הסחלב אינן מובנות היטב", אומר מר סטנביק. בעוד היעדר חלקים מעל פני הקרקע של הסחלב חוסך במים, הלחצים האבולוציוניים שהובילו להתאמה זו נותרים נושא למחקר.  שלושה מיני סחלבים נוספים נטולי כלורופיל קיימים באוסטרליה, שניים במערב אוסטרליה ואחד נוסף במדינות המזרחיות. זהו המין הראשון שנשלח להולנד לבדיקות גנטיות, אם כי גם מין אחר נדגם ה-DNA שלו. בעוד שסחלבים תת קרקעיים כאלה נמצאים ברחבי העולם, מר סטנביק מציין את נדירותם היחסית.

article_content: After serving as the American ambassador to Russia since January 2012, Michael McFaul announced his resignation, effective shortly after the conclusion of the Sochi Winter Olympics.  A key architect of the Obama administration's attempt to 'reset' relations with Russia, McFaul's time in Moscow was marked by both diplomatic achievements and strained relations.  While he expressed fondness for the role and a deep appreciation for the opportunity to represent his country, McFaul cited the need to reunite with his family as the primary reason for his departure. His family returned to California last summer due to his eldest son's desire to finish high school there, making the long-distance arrangement unsustainable.  McFaul's tenure saw the signing of the New START arms control agreement and a transit treaty facilitating US and NATO access to Afghanistan through Russian territory. However, he also faced considerable scrutiny from some Russian media outlets, who questioned his motives and portrayed him as a supporter of opposition groups. This coincided with a period of heightened tension between the two nations, exacerbated by disagreements over the Syrian civil war and Edward Snowden's asylum in Russia. Prior to his ambassadorship, McFaul, a Stanford University political science professor, served as an advisor to then-Senator Barack Obama and later as senior director for Russia and Eurasian affairs at the National Security Council.  Deputy National Security Advisor Ben Rhodes acknowledged McFaul's significant contributions to American foreign policy during his five years of service.

article_content: 'Following a three-week delay, an FBI team, accompanied by U.S. military personnel, arrived in Benghazi to investigate the consulate attack that claimed the lives of four Americans, including Ambassador J. Christopher Stevens.  Attorney General Eric Holder emphasized that the investigation extended beyond Benghazi, with efforts both domestically and internationally.  Pentagon spokesman George Little confirmed the military support, stating the team spent several hours in the city.  He added that investigators were actively pursuing leads. Special Operations forces were also involved in intelligence gathering efforts in Libya and neighboring countries.  The delay was attributed to security concerns, necessitating military protection for the FBI team.  The attack, initially perceived as a spontaneous protest in response to an anti-Islam video, is now considered a pre-planned terrorist assault, potentially linked to al Qaeda, according to revised intelligence assessments.  The discovery of sensitive documents at the unsecured compound following the attack raised questions about the investigation's integrity.'

article_content: 'A hospital in Northwest Indiana discharged the first American diagnosed with MERS after a full recovery. Health officials confirmed the patient is no longer a threat to public health and is free to travel.  Multiple tests conducted by the Indiana State Department of Health and the CDC showed no signs of active infection. The patient, an American man, had traveled from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, via London to Chicago on April 24th.  After arriving in Indiana, he sought treatment at Community Hospital in Munster on April 28th with symptoms including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. While MERS is a member of the coronavirus family, which also includes the common cold and SARS, it's not as contagious as influenza or measles. Although the virus has a high mortality rate, there's no specific treatment other than addressing symptoms. Around fifty hospital employees who interacted with the patient before the diagnosis are being monitored at home and will remain off-duty until the incubation period ends and negative test results are confirmed. No other MERS cases have been reported.'
